findings.original: In the year 1861 the population alone of the town centres of this industry in Great Britain numbered 101,302.
findings.rewrite: In the year 1861 the population of the town centers of this industry in Great Britain alone numbered 101,302.
findings.problem: Moving "alone" shifts its scope from "just the town centers" (as against the wider trade Wedgwood counted) to "Great Britain alone" (as against other countries), which is not Marx's restriction.
findings.fix: In the year 1861 the population of just the town centers of this industry in Great Britain numbered 101,302.

notes_review: The logged calls are sound: leaving the relative-surplus-population explanation out is right because p117 is the manufacturers' scare-quoted term and p121 gives Marx's own definition, and the literal Latin glosses in [^72] and p115 follow §2.3 while keeping the source's sense.
summary: Fidelity is very high: the Cairnes, Ferrand and Redgrave quotations are verbatim, irony and the Après moi le déluge passage survive intact, and only one misplaced "alone" in p115 changes a qualification. Readability is good, with long periodic sentences split cleanly and no padding.
